req.title: Register form html served
req.statement: The system shall include HTML input fields named 'username' and 'password' in the /auth/register page.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-027 requires that GET /auth/register returns an HTTP 2xx response containing HTML input fields named 'username' and 'password'. Three tests are designed: (1) positive EP test verifying status 200 and both named input fields present in the response body; (2) negative NEG test verifying that a wrong HTTP method (POST with no data) does NOT satisfy the 'form served' contract — the page re-renders with 200 but we assert the field names still appear (mutation: if field names were stripped on POST re-render, this catches it); (3) boundary BVA test verifying the exact byte-level presence of name="username" and name="password" attributes, catching mutations that alter the attribute name strings. Each test is self-contained, uses in-process Flask test client, and makes exact-value assertions to maximise mutation kill rate.

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_register_get_returns_200_with_username_and_password_fields():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/auth/register')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'name="username"' in r.data
    assert b'name="password"' in r.data

test_register_get_returns_200_with_username_and_password_fields()

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_register_html_contains_exact_input_name_attributes():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/auth/register')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    html = r.data
    assert b'name="username"' in html
    assert b'name="password"' in html
    assert b'name="user"' not in html or b'name="username"' in html
    assert b'name="passwd"' not in html or b'name="password"' in html
    assert html.count(b'name="username"') >= 1
    assert html.count(b'name="password"') >= 1

test_register_html_contains_exact_input_name_attributes()
